descriptionChirho: Proper noun designating Iddo (עִדּוֹ), a prophetic figure and chronicler referenced in post-exilic literature (2 Chr 9:29, 12:15, 13:22; Ezra 5:1, 6:14; Zech 1:1, 7; Neh 12:4, 16). All three clusters refer to the same individual in varying syntactic frames: bare nominative or with preposition 'to Iddo' (S122520), conjunction-prefixed 'and Iddo' (S122521), and a ketiv variant with preposition (S122522). Multilingual translations consistently identify one person: Spanish 'Ido / Idó,' Hindi 'इद्दो,' Arabic 'عِدُّو / عِدّو / عَدّايا,' Korean '잇도,' Swahili 'Ido.' The ketiv reading in S122522 (possibly עַדָּיָא/Adya) is a textual variant of the same referent.
